newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian First Bank signals good prospects.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian First Bank signals good prospects.

text.p: An improved full year profit at First Bank of Nigeria suggests that the recent distress in the banking sector may be easing, analysts said on Tuesday.
The bank, Nigeria's oldest, on Monday posted after-tax profits of 1.2 billion naira for 1996 against 1.00 billion naira a year earlier.
Analysts and stockbrokers hailed the result, saying it showed brighter prospects lay ahead for the sector as a whole.
"It shows the banks are in a healthy state and the bogey of distress is no longer threatening," one said.
A string of bad debts and fraud put many Nigerian banks in distress three years ago.
General Sani Abacha's military government stepped in with tough measures, including the jailing of bank executives and bad debtors, which have brought some sanity, according to analysts.
"The banks now have a lot of cash in their vaults," said Azubuike Okpalaoka of TRW Stockbrokers. "They have recovered a lot of their debts."
Bankers said Abacha's efforts had helped to clean up the system, ensuring that the fear of distress no longer bothered investors.
"Essentially, many unscrupulous people who came into the sector some years ago with the aim of making money from the banks rather than for them have now been flushed out," said Okpalaoka.

Banker Onah Aigbokhan said First Bank had made money from a new service called Western Union Money Transfer which allows Nigerians resident abroad to send money home electronically through its branches.
One other stabilising measure was the government's directive in the 1997 budget that banks raise their capital base nine-fold to 500 million naira by end-1998.
First Bank said gross earnings rose to 10.9 billion naira in the 1996 financial year from 8.9 billion naira the year before.
Pre-tax profit also jumped 1.3 billion naira from 1.2 billion naira. A dividend of 56 kobo per share and a scrip of one new share for four were also proposed.
Okpalaoka said bank shares would continue to be profitable for investors who did not sell during the difficult period but he said new ones would probably be entering late.
First Bank's shares appreciated almost three-fold from late last year to Tuesday when they were adjusted for the proposed dividend and scrip, dealers said.
When Britain's Standard Chartered Bank divested its 9.9 percent holding in the bank last year, the stock cost 7.00 naira, rising to 20.60 naira this month before closing at 20.20 naira on Monday.
It closed at 15.71 naira on Tuesday after the adjustment for the proposed dividend and scrip.
